# US-China Trade War: Tariffs, Trade Volumes, and Supply Chain Shifts (2016–2024)

## Overview
This collection of datasets tracks the evolution of the US-China trade war from 2016 to 2024, covering tariff rate changes, bilateral trade volumes, supply chain diversification patterns, and key policy milestones.

## Data Source

### tariff_rates
Average effective tariff rates by half-year period (2017-H1 to 2024-H1). Fields: `period` (string, format YYYY-HX), `us_tariff_on_china` (percent, range 3.1–25.4), `china_tariff_on_us` (percent, range 8.0–23.1). Rates represent trade-weighted averages across all tariff lines.

### bilateral_trade
Annual US-China bilateral trade from 2016 to 2024. Fields: `year` (integer), `us_exports_to_china` (billion USD), `us_imports_from_china` (billion USD), `total_bilateral` (billion USD, sum of exports and imports).

### supply_chain_share
Annual share of total US goods imports by source. Fields: `year` (integer), `china` (percent), `vietnam` (percent), `india` (percent), `rest_of_world` (percent). Values for each year sum to approximately 100%.

### policy_events
Key policy milestones. Fields: `date` (ISO date string), `period_approx` (corresponding half-year period), `event` (short description), `category` (one of: investigation, tariff, deal, review). Contains 12 events spanning August 2017 to May 2024.

## Data Notes
- Tariff rates are approximate trade-weighted averages and may differ from statutory rates on specific product categories
- 2024 data is partial (H1 only for tariffs; full-year trade figures are estimates)
- Supply chain shares are rounded and may not sum to exactly 100%
- Rest-of-world is a residual category capturing all non-China, non-Vietnam, non-India imports

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.dates as mdates
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch
import numpy as np
from datetime import datetime

# ── Data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
tariff_data = [
    ("2017-H1", 3.1, 8.0), ("2017-H2", 3.1, 8.0),
    ("2018-H1", 3.8, 8.0), ("2018-H2", 12.0, 16.5),
    ("2019-H1", 18.3, 20.7), ("2019-H2", 21.0, 21.8),
    ("2020-H1", 19.3, 20.9), ("2020-H2", 19.3, 20.9),
    ("2021-H1", 19.3, 20.9), ("2021-H2", 19.3, 20.9),
    ("2022-H1", 19.3, 21.1), ("2022-H2", 19.3, 21.1),
    ("2023-H1", 19.3, 21.2), ("2023-H2", 19.3, 21.2),
    ("2024-H1", 25.4, 23.1),
]

trade_data = [
    (2016, 115.6, 462.6, 578.2), (2017, 129.9, 505.5, 635.4),
    (2018, 120.3, 539.5, 659.8), (2019, 106.4, 452.2, 558.6),
    (2020, 124.5, 435.4, 559.9), (2021, 151.1, 506.4, 657.5),
    (2022, 153.8, 536.8, 690.6), (2023, 147.8, 427.2, 575.0),
    (2024, 138.2, 401.5, 539.7),
]

supply_data = [
    (2016, 21.4, 2.1, 2.1, 74.4), (2017, 21.6, 2.2, 2.2, 74.0),
    (2018, 21.2, 2.6, 2.3, 73.9), (2019, 18.1, 2.9, 2.4, 76.6),
    (2020, 18.6, 3.4, 2.3, 75.7), (2021, 17.9, 3.7, 2.7, 75.7),
    (2022, 16.5, 3.9, 2.8, 76.8), (2023, 13.9, 4.5, 3.1, 78.5),
    (2024, 12.8, 4.9, 3.4, 78.9),
]

policy_events = [
    ("2017-08-14", "Section 301\nInvestigation", "investigation"),
    ("2018-03-22", "Section 301\nMemo ($50B)", "tariff"),
    ("2018-07-06", "List 1 Tariffs\n$34B", "tariff"),
    ("2018-08-23", "List 2 Tariffs\n$16B", "tariff"),
    ("2018-09-24", "List 3 Tariffs\n$200B", "tariff"),
    ("2019-05-10", "List 3 → 25%\n$200B", "tariff"),
    ("2019-09-01", "List 4A Tariffs\n$112B", "tariff"),
    ("2020-01-15", "Phase One\nDeal Signed", "deal"),
    ("2020-02-14", "Phase One\nCuts Take Effect", "deal"),
    ("2021-10-04", "USTR Tariff\nReview", "review"),
    ("2022-06-20", "Biden Considers\nExclusions", "review"),
    ("2024-05-14", "Biden EV/Semi\nTariff Hikes", "tariff"),
]

# ── Convert to arrays ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def half_year_to_float(period):
    year, half = period.split("-H")
    return int(year) + (0.0 if half == "1" else 0.5)

tariff_x = np.array([half_year_to_float(d[0]) for d in tariff_data])
us_tariff = np.array([d[1] for d in tariff_data])
cn_tariff = np.array([d[2] for d in tariff_data])

trade_years = np.array([d[0] for d in trade_data])
us_exports = np.array([d[1] for d in trade_data])
us_imports = np.array([d[2] for d in trade_data])
total_trade = np.array([d[3] for d in trade_data])

supply_years = np.array([d[0] for d in supply_data])
china_share = np.array([d[1] for d in supply_data])
vietnam_share = np.array([d[2] for d in supply_data])
india_share = np.array([d[3] for d in supply_data])
row_share = np.array([d[4] for d in supply_data])

event_dates = [datetime.strptime(e[0], "%Y-%m-%d") for e in policy_events]
event_labels = [e[1] for e in policy_events]
event_cats = [e[2] for e in policy_events]
event_x = [d.year + (d.month - 1) / 12 for d in event_dates]

# ── Color palette (editorial, publication-ready) ─────────────────────────────
US_TARIFF_COLOR = "#B71C1C"
CN_TARIFF_COLOR = "#0D47A1"
US_EXPORT_COLOR = "#5C6BC0"
US_IMPORT_COLOR = "#E57373"
TOTAL_TRADE_COLOR = "#263238"
CHINA_SHARE_COLOR = "#C62828"
VIETNAM_SHARE_COLOR = "#2E7D32"
INDIA_SHARE_COLOR = "#E65100"
ROW_SHARE_COLOR = "#CFD8DC"
BG_COLOR = "#FAFAFA"
GRID_COLOR = "#E0E0E0"
SPINE_COLOR = "#9E9E9E"
EVENT_COLORS = {
    "tariff": "#D32F2F",
    "deal": "#1976D2",
    "review": "#7B1FA2",
    "investigation": "#F57F17",
}

# ── Figure setup ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 14), facecolor=BG_COLOR)
fig.subplots_adjust(hspace=0.12, left=0.09, right=0.92, top=0.93, bottom=0.05)

ax1 = fig.add_axes([0.09, 0.68, 0.83, 0.24])   # Tariffs
ax2 = fig.add_axes([0.09, 0.38, 0.83, 0.24])   # Trade volumes
ax3 = fig.add_axes([0.09, 0.05, 0.83, 0.27])   # Supply chain

for ax in [ax1, ax2, ax3]:
    ax.set_facecolor(BG_COLOR)
    ax.tick_params(colors="#424242", labelsize=9)
    for spine in ax.spines.values():
        spine.set_color(SPINE_COLOR)
        spine.set_linewidth(0.5)

# ── Title ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig.suptitle(
    "US–China Trade War: Tariffs, Trade Volumes & Supply Chain Shifts (2016–2024)",
    fontsize=16, fontweight="bold", color="#212121", x=0.50, y=0.97
)
fig.text(0.50, 0.945, "Average effective tariff rates, bilateral trade, and US import source shares with key policy milestones",
         fontsize=9, color="#616161", ha="center", va="top")

# ── Panel 1: Tariff Escalation ────────────────────────────────────────────────
ax1.step(tariff_x, us_tariff, where='mid', color=US_TARIFF_COLOR, linewidth=2.2,
         label="US tariff on Chinese goods", zorder=3)
ax1.step(tariff_x, cn_tariff, where='mid', color=CN_TARIFF_COLOR, linewidth=2.2,
         label="China tariff on US goods", zorder=3)
ax1.fill_between(tariff_x, us_tariff, step='mid', alpha=0.08, color=US_TARIFF_COLOR)
ax1.fill_between(tariff_x, cn_tariff, step='mid', alpha=0.08, color=CN_TARIFF_COLOR)

# Policy event markers on Panel 1
annotated_positions = []
for i, (ex, el, ec) in enumerate(zip(event_x, event_labels, event_cats)):
    color = EVENT_COLORS.get(ec, "#757575")
    ax1.axvline(x=ex, color=color, linewidth=0.7, alpha=0.5, linestyle='--', zorder=1)

    # Stagger label positions to reduce overlap
    y_pos = 28 + (i % 3) * 3.5
    ax1.annotate(
        el, xy=(ex, 26.5), xytext=(ex, y_pos),
        fontsize=6.2, color=color, fontweight='bold',
        ha='center', va='bottom',
        arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-', color=color, lw=0.5),
        zorder=5,
    )

ax1.set_ylabel("Effective Tariff Rate (%)", fontsize=10, color="#424242", fontweight='medium')
ax1.set_xlim(2016.5, 2024.7)
ax1.set_ylim(0, 38)
ax1.set_xticks([])
ax1.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FormatStrFormatter('%.0f%%'))
ax1.grid(axis='y', color=GRID_COLOR, linewidth=0.5, zorder=0)
ax1.legend(loc='upper left', fontsize=8.5, framealpha=0.9, edgecolor=SPINE_COLOR)

# Panel label
ax1.text(2016.65, 36.5, "A", fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', color="#212121",
         bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.2', facecolor='#E0E0E0', edgecolor='none'))

# Shade escalation period
ax1.axvspan(2018.0, 2020.0, alpha=0.06, color='#FF6F00', zorder=0)
ax1.text(2019.0, 1.5, "Peak Escalation Phase", fontsize=7, color='#E65100',
         ha='center', fontstyle='italic', alpha=0.8)

ax2.fill_between(trade_years, us_imports, alpha=0.25, color=US_IMPORT_COLOR, zorder=2)
ax2.fill_between(trade_years, us_exports, alpha=0.25, color=US_EXPORT_COLOR, zorder=2)
ax2.plot(trade_years, us_imports, color=US_IMPORT_COLOR, linewidth=2, marker='o',
         markersize=5, label="US Imports from China", zorder=3)
ax2.plot(trade_years, us_exports, color=US_EXPORT_COLOR, linewidth=2, marker='s',
         markersize=5, label="US Exports to China", zorder=3)
ax2.plot(trade_years, total_trade, color=TOTAL_TRADE_COLOR, linewidth=2.5,
         marker='D', markersize=5, label="Total Bilateral Trade", zorder=4, linestyle='-')

# Add value labels for key points
for yr, val in zip(trade_years, total_trade):
    if yr in [2016, 2018, 2019, 2022, 2024]:
        offset = 18 if yr != 2019 else -25
        ax2.annotate(f"${val:.0f}B", xy=(yr, val), xytext=(0, offset),
                     textcoords='offset points', fontsize=7, color=TOTAL_TRADE_COLOR,
                     ha='center', fontweight='bold', zorder=5)

# Highlight dip
min_idx = np.argmin(total_trade[3:]) + 3  # skip first 3 years
ax2.annotate("Trade dip during\npeak tariffs",
             xy=(trade_years[min_idx], total_trade[min_idx]),
             xytext=(trade_years[min_idx] + 1.3, total_trade[min_idx] - 15),
             fontsize=7.5, color="#B71C1C", fontstyle='italic',
             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#B71C1C', lw=1.2),
             zorder=5)

# Policy event lines (lighter on this panel)

    color = EVENT_COLORS.get(ec, "#757575")
    ax2.axvline(x=ex, color=color, linewidth=0.4, alpha=0.3, linestyle=':', zorder=1)

ax2.set_xlim(2016.5, 2024.7)
